newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Jospin not going to G7 in Denver.
newsitem.headline: France's Jospin not going to G7 in Denver.

text.p: French Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin has decided against accompanying conservative President Jacques Chirac to a Denver meeting of the Group of Seven industrialised nations, Jospin aides said on Thursday.

Jospin had initially said he would go with Chirac to major international meetings as part of their sharing of power following the left's upset victory in a June 1 parliamentary election but later said he had not yet decided about next week's G7 meeting in Denver.
The meeting is to begin on June 20, a day after Jospin is due to deliver his first major policy address to parliament, outlining his political programme.
Jospin and Chirac have been warily circling each other since the left took power last week, anxious to mark out their respective turf without causing sparks or outright conflicts.

Under the French constitution, the president signs treaties and guarantees their observance and is commander in chief of the armed forces, but the goverment determines and conducts the nation's policy, including on defence.

In related developments, Jospin's office announced that the prime minister would talk to his British counterpart Tony Blair later on Thursday and would confer with Chirac on Saturday evening, in preparation for a June 16-17 European Union summit in Amsterdam.
